$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §2 (identity), §3 (coordinates), §4 (c14n, and geometry excluded from the fingerprint), §5 (locators and typed absence), §6 (derivation), §7 (the L1 gate), §11 (the grounding projection). Written from crates/ethos-parser-core/src/representation.rs. THE RECORD, not a projection: ethos.grounding.v1 is derived from this and is deliberately lossy, so a grounding round-trip is never proof this is intact.
title: DocumentRepresentation v0 (DRAFT)
description: The canonical evidence record: what was read, who read it, under what pinned configuration, what they could not do, and every ordered typed node with its required native address.

artifact_type.$comment: At the TOP LEVEL, before any payload (§2), so a reader can fail closed on an unrecognised shape before parsing it (§8). Mirrors representation.identity.artifact_type, and a parse-time check refuses an artifact where the two disagree — a mirror that can disagree is worse than no mirror.

representation.$comment: THE HASHED SUBTREE. representation_c14n_sha256 is the digest of exactly this member and nothing else.

representation_c14n_sha256.$comment: REPRESENTATION identity, distinct from source identity (§2) and — importantly — distinct from Ethos's field of the same name, which is a hash of a grounding FILE's raw bytes. Computed as `"sha256:" + hex(sha256(c14n(doc["representation"])))`. The hashed bytes are a literal subtree rather than the document minus a named key set, because an exclusion rule is a second canonicalization contract two implementations can drift on, and a drifted rule produces a mismatch that looks exactly like tampering. NOT checked at parse time, deliberately: a validator that refuses to load the artifact it is judging can only ever report 'invalid JSON', where the report shape distinguishes structure from binding. `ethos-parser ground` calls verify_fingerprint() before projecting.

geometry.$comment: OUTSIDE the fingerprint, by §4: rectangles are preserved for display and inspection but are not fingerprint-critical, because text is anchored by stable origin locators rather than boxes. Two independent PDF stacks agree on character origin to 0.001 pt and disagree on height by 6.174 pt — fingerprinting the boxes would make identity hostage to the least reliable number in the artifact. Implemented by keeping the type OUT of the payload rather than by filtering at hash time: a filter is a rule someone can quietly change, a type that is not there cannot be hashed by accident. Exactly one row per node, in node order; a missing row would make absence ambiguous with omission, so a misaligned sidecar is refused at parse.

source.description: SOURCE identity: the digest of the exact original bytes. What went in, as opposed to what came out.

media_type.$comment: `application/pdf` at v0, and one of nine since v2-S2: ethos-parser-office writes the other eight. NOT ethos.grounding.v1's source.media_type, which that schema pins to `application/pdf` — decision #16: a DOCX can bind to its source through this field and still cannot be grounded.

processing_run.$comment: The companion names a ProcessingRun/StageRun carrying processor, adapter, build and profile identities. v0 has one processor and one stage, so this is the honest subset — a `stages` array with a single hardcoded entry would be shape without information. NO RUN ID AND NO TIMESTAMP: either would make two runs over identical bytes under an identical profile produce different artifacts, and byte identity across runs is a test here. A run's identity is its inputs.

reading_order_rule.$comment: On the artifact so a reader need not fetch the profile. `gutter-columns-v2` (D4-S2) and `gutter-columns-v1` (v1-S5) order nodes by whitespace in page space: a two-column document reads column-major, and a page with no gutter is not reordered. `gutter-columns-v4` reads a page with no gutter top to bottom by the slabs its leading separates, keeping content-stream order inside each. `single-column-v1` means content-stream order, so a multi-column document is in the WRONG ORDER — which a profile naming it declares in assurance.limitations rather than hiding. Two artifacts under the two ids can list the same runs in a different sequence, so this string is part of reading them.

tables.$comment: v1-S1. Optional on the wire (`#[serde(default)]`) and always written. An empty array means the detector LOOKED and found none; `assurance.capabilities.tables` says whether it looked. Absent from this schema until 2026-09-24 while `additionalProperties` was already false, so this file described a payload the engine had not emitted since v1-S1.

outlines.$comment: docs/29-OUTLINES-SCOPE.md. The hierarchy a PDF catalog declares, one record per `/Outlines` entry, in `/First`/`/Next` order. Optional on the wire and always written: an empty array means the reader LOOKED and the catalog named none, and `assurance.capabilities.outlines` says whether it looked. Never `nodes`: a bookmark title is text no content stream painted, so it has no native locator and North Star #4 requires one on every node.

figures.$comment: Decision #46, docs/34-FIGURE-REGIONS-SCOPE.md. The regions `figure-regions-v1` infers from the paths a page paints, in page order. Optional on the wire and always written: an empty array means the rule found none, or did not run on a document that declares author structure, and `assurance.capabilities.figures` says whether the profile runs it at all. Never `nodes`: a region claims no text, and the runs inside it are nodes already.

assurance.$comment: M4's L1 gate, carried forward by value: capabilities, limitations, per-page state, coverage, terminal state. An artifact without it has not reached 'extracted' regardless of how good its text is.

page_record.title: A page — a record, deliberately NOT a node
page_record.$comment: A node carries a required NativeLocator, and the PDF variant of that is a CHARACTER origin. A page has none, so making a page a node would force the emitter to write an origin it does not have — and {"origin_x":0,"origin_y":0} for a page is indistinguishable on the wire from a run drawn in the corner. Inventing a coordinate is forbidden outright (§5.2, Workbench rule 3). One extra array removes the temptation entirely.

index.$comment: The DOCUMENT'S OWN 1-based page number, not this record's position in the array. The two differ the moment a page is quarantined or fails, and a citation renders against the document's number.

id.$comment: Stable within this representation AND this profile, never globally. A profile upgrade creates a new representation plus a mapping, rather than pretending node ids are permanently global. The grounding projection reuses this id for its span, so a consumer can join a span back to its node without a mapping table.

kind.$comment: `text_run` is NOT a line and NOT a paragraph: a PDF run is exactly what the content stream drew in one operation, and an office run is the smallest unit its format writes, so calling either a block would be a claim about layout that no code makes. `form_field` and `annotation` are PDF objects read since v1-S4, and `image` a painted XObject since v1-S6; every office node is a `text_run`, told apart by its attributes. Constrained to ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$ because this spelling becomes the grounding artifact's `kind` verbatim.

parent.$comment: For a paginated format, the id of the page record this node was drawn on. For a page-less one, the id of the part it was read from, one id per part the locators name, and one for an RTF's single stream.

ordinal.$comment: 1-based and contiguous within a page, in reading order. Refused at parse if it is not.

native_locator.title: NativeLocator — required on every node (§5.1)
native_locator.$comment: A discriminated union: adding a format adds a variant, plus an adapter profile, fixtures and inspection behaviour. It does not change the source, run, artifact or verification models. Externally tagged so a new variant is additive and an unrecognised one fails closed: exactly one key, naming the variant. Lives in ethos-parser-core because the union is part of the CONTRACT — see docs/04-ARCHITECTURE.md §1 on machinery versus vocabulary. ethos-parser-grounding never reads one. The three PDF variants address a page; the eight office ones address a part and positions in it, and none carries a page, a box or a coordinate (docs/history/14-V2-SCOPE.md §3).

part.$comment: The package's own name for the part, verbatim.

paragraph.$comment: 1-based position of the <w:p> in the part's document order.

run.$comment: 1-based position of the <w:r> within that paragraph.

part.$comment: The package's name for the worksheet.

sheet.$comment: The workbook's name for it, as <sheet name> writes it: what a person citing a cell writes down.

row.$comment: The row as the file numbers it: the digits of <c r="B12">.

column.$comment: The column as the file spells it: the letters of <c r="B12">.

shape.$comment: 1-based position of the <p:sp> within the part.

paragraph.$comment: 1-based position of the <a:p> within that shape's <p:txBody>.

run.$comment: 1-based position of the <a:r> within that paragraph.

paragraph.$comment: 1-based position of the <text:p> or <text:h> in the part's document order.

row.$comment: 1-based position of the row within its table, counting table:number-rows-repeated.

column.$comment: 1-based position of the cell within its row, counting table:number-columns-repeated. A number, not a letter: OpenDocument writes neither.

draw_page.$comment: 1-based position of the <draw:page> in the part's document order. A position among elements the file lists, never a page this engine measured.

shape.$comment: 1-based position of the shape within that draw page.

paragraph.$comment: 1-based position of the <text:p> or <text:h> within that shape.
1-based position of the paragraph in the stream's own order. No part: an RTF is one byte stream, and a constant standing in for a part it does not have would be invented.

part.$comment: The spine item's path in the package.

block.$comment: 1-based position of the block within that spine document.

pdf_locator.title: A glyph run's address: page, baseline origin, advance

advance.$comment: OMITTED, not zero, when the document carries no widths. Absent means the reader does not know.

pdf_object_locator.title: A PDF object's address: page, object id, and the rectangle it declares (v1-S4)
pdf_object_locator.$comment: An annotation or a form field has no baseline, no advance and no character origin, so the glyph-run variant is the wrong shape for it. An object id is both halves.

rect.$comment: What the author wrote in /Rect: a rectangle, nothing, or something that is not one.

pdf_image_locator.title: A painted image's address: page, XObject id, and the rectangle the Do filled (v1-S6)
pdf_image_locator.$comment: Its own variant because the rectangle means something else: an annotation's /Rect is a number the author wrote, and an image's is COMPUTED — the current transformation matrix applied to the unit square.

structural_locator.title: StructuralLocator — where the node kind defines one
structural_locator.$comment: Externally tagged, one of three variants, matching StructuralLocator in crates/ethos-parser-core/src/representation.rs. The tagged-structure tree has been READ since v1-S3 (struct-tree-v1): pdf_tagged is the address the document's own /StructTreeRoot gives the content, pdf_mcid an id the content stream supplied that no structure element claims, pdf_artifact content the page marked as furniture outside the tree. pdf_tagged.derivation is read since auto-tagging S1 (struct-tree-v2): `extracted` when the innermost citing element is the author's, `computed` when it carries this engine's own owner attribute (/O /EthosParser under /A, or through /C and the root's /ClassMap; docs/23-AUTO-TAGGING-SCOPE.md §4.2), written on every tagged locator with no default (decision #20). Omitted entirely when the page marked nothing; never invented.

pdf_mcid.$comment: Captured verbatim from BDC, and NO structure element claims it: either the document has no tree, or it has one and this id is not in it. The assurance block's limitations say which.

mcid.$comment: The marked-content id the tree cited to reach this content. -1 on a node the tree cites by /OBJR rather than by marked content (an annotation or a widget): no id is involved, and a non-negative value here would be one this engine minted.

role_path.$comment: Structure types from the root down, exactly as the document wrote them in /S. Never laundered.

standard_role_path.$comment: The same path after the document's own /RoleMap. Present only when the map changed something.

element_id.$comment: The innermost element's /ID, when it declares one. Never minted.

derivation.$comment: `extracted` or `computed` — see the $comment on this def. Required and never defaulted.

mcid.$comment: Present only when the artifact sequence carried an id, which it usually does not.

pdf_artifact.$comment: Content the page marked /Artifact (PDF 32000-1 §14.8.2.2): running heads, folios, rules. Flagged, never dropped.

text_run_attributes.$comment: A typed struct rather than an open map: an open map is a place for a future field to arrive unreviewed, and additionalProperties:false cannot police one. NONE of these survives the grounding projection — a lossiness test enumerates them.

scalar_code_mismatch.$comment: True when text.chars().count() != char_codes.len(). A ligature is one code and several scalars. Declared, not reconciled.

synthesized.description: Characters this reader inserted. Empty for text taken verbatim.

font_size.$comment: Integer centipoints. NEVER used as a box height.

findings.$comment: v1-S6. What was OBSERVED about this run, never a judgement about it: `invisible-render-mode` means the run was drawn in text rendering mode 3 or 7, which is how an OCR layer is laid under a scan AND how text is hidden from a reader — this profile reports the mode and does not decide which it is looking at. `off-page` means the origin lies outside /CropBox, or /MediaBox where no crop box is declared, after /Rotate. Findings are ADDITIVE: a node carrying one is still emitted with its text, origin and locator intact, and no finding removes anything. Sorted and deduplicated, so two artifacts about one run cannot differ by the order two observations happened in. Omitted when empty, which is almost every run. The same code appears in assurance.limitations as a document-level count; the two are one observation seen twice.
findings.description: Observations about this run. Never a reason to drop it.

region.$comment: D4-S2. Which region of its page the reading-order cut placed this run in, 1-based, in reading order. WHERE text sits, never WHAT it is: not a paragraph, a heading or a column name, and no role may be read from it (P14 — roles come from the structure tree or from nowhere). ABSENT means the cut made no division, which is not the same claim as 'single column'; the profile's reading_order_rule says which rule ran, and under `single-column-v1` no cut runs at all. Absent on almost every page, which is why it is omitted rather than emitted as null.

block.$comment: Which block of its page the leading-gap cut placed this run in, 1-based, in reading order. Emitted under reading_order_rule `gutter-columns-v3` and `gutter-columns-v4`, and absent under every earlier id. WHERE text sits, never WHAT it is: a block is a stretch separated from its neighbours by vertical whitespace wider than its band's own leading, and it is NOT a paragraph, a heading, a list item or a section. No role may be read from it (P14 — roles come from the structure tree or from nowhere), and doc 19 §6 permits this field only as an unnamed Computed index. IT IS NOT A PARAGRAPH INDEX, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO: on the one gate document able to carry a real paragraph label the rule finds 63.7% of real breaks at 100% precision — it never fires mid-paragraph across 719 chances, and it misses better than a third of the breaks, because 35.1% of real breaks carry no extra leading for any gap rule to see. ABSENT means the rule declined, and unlike region that is the ORDINARY case: a page of uniform body text has no gap wide enough to open a second block and is supposed to have none. Absent also covers a band whose modal gap is a table-column interleave pitch rather than a leading, a band whose gaps are a scatter with no mode, and a format with no cut.

layout_unit.$comment: Decision #38. Which layout unit of its page the profile's layout_unit_rule joined this run's line into, 1-based in reading order: consecutive lines set no more than half a line apart, overlapping across, of one kind (body text, or an inferred heading of one level), the next opening no list marker; under `line-units-v2` cut where a piece of the line (its runs, cut at gaps wider than its height) follows one that ends short — more than ten of its heights left of the unit's widest piece — so a line's label and value can be two units. WHERE, NEVER WHAT, as block is: a unit is not the author's paragraph and no role is read from it. ABSENT on a document that declares author structure, on a table's runs and an /Artifact's, on a whitespace-only line, and under every other rule id.

inferred_heading.$comment: Decision #29. Set where the profile's heading_inference_rule read this run's line as a heading from the TYPE THE PAGE DRAWS, on a document that declares no /StructTreeRoot. Computed, never the author's: the rule id names the rule, and the artifact declares headings-inferred-from-type with the line count and the body reference in centipoints it measured. ABSENT WHERE FALSE — hence `const: true` — so a run the rule did not touch serializes exactly as it did before the rule existed, and a tagged document's artifact differs only by the profile hash. A verdict and not a measurement: the rendered em it was read from exists only inside the PDF reader, and is not on the wire. Only a text run can carry it, so no office node can acquire an inferred heading by accident.

inferred_heading_level.$comment: Decision #38. The level `type-size-v3` gave an inferred heading, where it is deeper than 1: the sizes a document's inferred headings are set in, largest first, are levels 1 to 6, and a bold line standing apart is the level below the smallest. Computed, as inferred_heading is, and only beside it. ABSENT AT LEVEL 1 and on every run that is no inferred heading, so a document whose headings share one size serializes as it did under `type-size-v2`.

bold.$comment: Decision #38. Set where the font that drew this run declares itself bold — a /FontWeight of 600 or more, the ForceBold flag, or a bold style word in its /BaseFont — under the profile's observation_rule `page-observations-v3`. A statement about the typeface, rendered as strong emphasis by the projections. PDF only. Absent where false.

italic.$comment: Decision #38. Set where the font that drew this run declares itself italic — the Italic flag, or Italic or Oblique in its /BaseFont. As bold. Absent where false.

script.$comment: Decision #40. The run is set as a superscript (raised) or a subscript (lowered): six characters or fewer, at most nine tenths the em of a run beside it on another baseline, and off that baseline by a tenth to half that run's em. Computed from where the runs sit, under the profile's observation_rule `page-observations-v3`; the projections write <sup> and <sub>. PDF only. Absent on a run set on its line.

furniture.$comment: Decision #41. The run's line is page furniture: in its page's first (header) or last (footer) band of lines, set apart from the rest by half a body line or more and lying wholly inside the page's outer tenth, a band holding no table. Computed from where the page's lines sit, under the profile's furniture_rule `margin-bands-v1`; WHERE, NEVER WHAT WAS MEANT: a running head and a page title set apart read alike, and the run stays in the text and every projection. PDF only. ABSENT on a document that declares author structure, on every other line, and under every other rule id.

node_attributes.title: NodeAttributes — the kind-specific fields of a node
node_attributes.$comment: Externally tagged, exactly one key, like native_locator: a new variant is additive and an unrecognised one fails closed. `text_run`, `form_field`, `annotation` and `image` are the PDF reader's; the other eight are one per office format family, each on a `text_run` node.

space_preserved.$comment: DOCX: whether the run's <w:t> carried xml:space="preserve".

value_type.$comment: XLSX: the type the cell's t attribute states.

text_source.$comment: Where the node's text came from: the stored value, the cached result of a formula, or the formula itself.

outline_level.$comment: ODT: a heading's text:outline-level, when it states one.

draw_page_name.$comment: ODP: the draw page's draw:name, when it has one.

shape_name.$comment: The shape's draw:name, when it has one.

terminator.$comment: Which control word ended the paragraph, or the end of the stream.

element.$comment: The XHTML element the block was read from.

linear.$comment: The spine itemref's linear attribute: false for an item outside the primary reading order.

odf_block_kind.$comment: Whether the ODF block was a <text:p> or a <text:h>.

field_name.$comment: The fully qualified name: the /T of every ancestor, root first, joined by `.`. Omitted when no /T appears anywhere up the chain.

field_type.$comment: /FT as the document spells it, from the nearest ancestor that declares one. Omitted when none does.

value.$comment: /V, typed by what the document wrote. A widget's rendering is never read as page text.

flags.$comment: The /Ff bits this profile recognises, named, in ascending bit order.

unrecognized_flag_bits.$comment: The raw /Ff bits this profile has no name for, kept rather than dropped. Omitted when there are none.

title.$comment: /T — conventionally the author — when the document gives one.

flags.$comment: The /F bits this profile recognises, named, in ascending bit order. A hidden annotation is flagged, never dropped.

unrecognized_flag_bits.$comment: The raw /F bits this profile has no name for. Omitted when there are none.

image_attributes.title: A painted image's attributes (v1-S6)
image_attributes.$comment: No description, caption or alt text: that would be OCR or a model's opinion, and neither is evidence.

stream_sha256.$comment: Digest of the XObject's stream bytes as the file stores them.

oneOf.$comment: The stored bytes are a file of this type on their own.
The bytes are samples only a PDF reader can decode.

table_record.title: A table, with its cells in slot order (v1-S1)

page.$comment: The id of the page record the table was found on.

derivation.$comment: `computed` for a grid this engine reconstructed from ink or alignment, `extracted` for one the structure tree declares.

detection_rule.$comment: The rule that produced this table, from profile.table_detection.

locator_check.$comment: The structural and geometric cross-check of the cells against the grid.

tagged_check.$comment: The detected grid compared with the /Table the structure tree describes on this page. OMITTED where the tree describes none, which is not the same claim as the two agreeing.

node_ids.$comment: The nodes whose text the cell holds, in reading order. Empty for an empty cell.

row.$comment: Zero-based row of the cell's top-left slot.

column.$comment: Zero-based column of the cell's top-left slot.

outcome.$comment: Internally tagged by `status`. A mismatch lists its faults rather than a verdict.

title.$comment: /Title decoded. Omitted, and counted, where it does not decode — never guessed.

depth.$comment: The depth the /First and /Next chain gives, 1 for a top-level entry. Never renumbered.

page.$comment: The page its destination resolves to, when it resolves. No end is ever emitted.
The id of the page record the region was found on.

geometry.$comment: Always `measured`: the union of the clustered paths' boxes, within the page.

derivation.$comment: Always `computed`: the paths are the document's, the grouping is this engine's.

detection_rule.$comment: The rule that drew the box, from profile.figure_rule.

node.$comment: The node id this row describes. Index-aligned with payload.nodes.

presence.$comment: Measured, or a typed reason there is none. A MEASURED box is additionally required to lie inside its page: a box outside is a HARD ERROR on construction, never a clamp and never an omission. Clamping fabricates a coordinate; omitting would have to travel the geometry-omission path, and that path takes a typed absence by construction — an out-of-page measured box is not an absence, and routing it through would be the 'omit for a non-geometry reason' hole §11 forbids.
